---
title: Running on GitHub
description: A library that lives in a repo and publishes itself, with nothing installed anywhere.
---

A library is a folder served on the web. A GitHub repo with Pages turned on is
exactly that, and GitHub Actions can run earmark on it. Put the two together and
you get a library you run from a browser. You list what you want to hear in one
file, commit it, and a few minutes later it is an episode in your podcast app.
There is no Python, no ffmpeg and no model download on your own machine.

## How it works

```
sources.yml  --commit-->  Action runs `earmark publish`  --commit-->  Pages serves feed.xml
```

- **`sources.yml`** is the reading list. It holds URLs, and files you have
  uploaded into the repo.
- **The earmark Action** runs [`earmark publish`](../reference/publish.qmd)
  with no SOURCE. That makes the feed match the list: new entries are narrated
  and published, and deleted entries are removed. The Action then commits the
  MP3s, the Markdown and the feed back to the repo.
- **GitHub Pages** serves that commit. Writing the MP3 is publishing it, as it
  is for any other library.

## Setting it up

1. Create a repo from the template
   [**earmark-dev/library-template**](https://github.com/earmark-dev/library-template)
   with **Use this template**. Make it **public**; see the limits below.
2. In the new repo, open **Settings → Pages**. Set *Source* to **Deploy from a
   branch**, branch `main`, folder `/ (root)`, then Save. This is the one step
   an Action cannot do for you.
3. Open the **Actions** tab, choose **earmark**, and click **Run workflow**.
   The first run writes `earmark.toml` with the right `base_url`, which is
   `https://<you>.github.io/<repo>`, and an empty feed.
4. The run's summary page shows the feed URL. Add it to your podcast app as a
   feed you add by URL; see [Subscribing on your phone](09-subscribing.qmd).

## Adding and removing things

Edit `sources.yml` in GitHub's web editor. The pencil icon works, including on
a phone:

```yaml
- https://example.com/an-article-i-meant-to-read
- files/attention-is-all-you-need.pdf
- source: https://example.com/a-long-read
  voice: bf_emma
```

For a PDF, a Word file or an EPUB, upload it into `files/` first
(**Add file → Upload files**), then list it. Committing starts the Action.

**To remove an episode, delete its line.** The next run removes the episode,
its MP3 and its Markdown. An entry is matched by its text exactly, so editing an
entry's `voice` does not re-narrate it. Delete the entry, commit, then add it
back.

The whole format is in the [configuration
reference](../reference/configuration.qmd#sources.yml). To change the voice,
speed or feed title for everything, edit `earmark.toml` as for any library.

## Using the Action in your own repo

The template is only a workflow that calls the Action. Any library repo can use
it directly:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/earmark.yml
on:
  push:
    paths: [sources.yml, "files/**", earmark.toml]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: write
concurrency:
  group: earmark
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: earmark-dev/earmark@v1
        # with:
        #   base-url: https://audio.example.com   # a custom domain
        #   title: My Reading Pile
```

`base-url` and `title` are only used on the first run, when there is no
`earmark.toml` yet. After that, `earmark.toml` is the only place settings live.

The Action caches the Kokoro model between runs, so the 354 MB download happens
once. A push made by the Action does not start another run, so committing back
cannot loop.

## Limits worth knowing

- **Everything in a public repo is public.** That includes every file in
  `files/` and every generated Markdown file. Only upload what you may
  redistribute. Pages on a private repo needs a paid GitHub plan, and a podcast
  app must still be able to fetch the feed without logging in.
- **One file may not pass 100 MB.** At the default 64 kbps that is about 3.4
  hours of audio. A longer book fails that run with a message; lower `bitrate`
  or split the document.
- **A Pages site stops at about 1 GB**, which is roughly 30 hours at the
  default bitrate. The run summary warns past 800 MB. Deleting entries from
  `sources.yml` is how you keep under it. `earmark feed --prune` is the wrong
  tool here, because a pruned episode that is still listed is re-narrated on
  the next run.
- **Actions runners are slower than a laptop.** Public repos get free minutes;
  private ones have a monthly allowance. A job may run for up to 6 hours, which
  is far more than any one article needs.
